title: A Parish for the Alibi Revisited
premise: Vesper Pemberton, a night-shift taxi dispatcher who hears the city's secrets through a headset, is hired by an anonymous client who pays triple rate to prove that a murder scheduled for the anniversary dinner of the Harrow family will not happen — because, the client insists, it hasn't happened yet. The case mirrors a killing from ten years ago that everyone in the parish swore was closed: Vesper's own father went to prison for it. As Vesper works backward from a murder that exists only as intention, they uncover a forged will, a found family of cab drivers and church volunteers protecting each other's alibis, and the truth that their father took the fall for someone he loved. The anniversary dinner becomes the stage where Vesper must expose the real killer — the family patriarch faking his own dementia to control the inheritance — before history repeats itself, ending with Vesper choosing justice outside the law over vindication inside it.
about_author: Petra Sandoval spent seven years answering phones at a 24-hour car service in a rust-belt city, where she learned that every fare has a story and half of them are lies. She writes mysteries about people the system overlooks, and this is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Vesper Pemberton, night dispatcher for Bellwether Cabs, takes an unusual booking: a client pays cash in advance for a driver to shadow the Harrow estate on the night of its tenth-anniversary dinner, 'to prove nothing happens.' Vesper's POV. The beat is wary curiosity — a lifetime of listening has taught them that prepaid silence always means something loud.

chapters.title: Ten Years Closed
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Vesper's father, Marcus, has served ten years for the murder of Eleanor Harrow, a case closed so neatly the parish stopped talking about it. Vesper visits him; he refuses to discuss the night it happened. Vesper's POV. Emotional beat: the ache of loving someone who chose prison over truth.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Vesper traces the payment to a defunct law office and a dead lawyer's letterhead. Someone is using a ghost to hire them. First-person investigation through dispatch logs and phone records. Vesper's POV. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession — the ghost knew details only the killer could know.

chapters.title: Parish of Small Alibis
chapters.summary: Introduction of the found family: Ruthie the church volunteer who feeds drivers, Okonkwo the veteran cabbie, and Deacon, a teenage runaway Vesper informally adopted. Each remembers fragments of the night Eleanor died. Rotating close-third POV begins with Ruthie. Beat: warmth that makes the coming danger personal.

chapters.title: What the Meter Recorded
chapters.summary: Vesper finds a decade-old dispatch tape showing a Bellwether cab at the Harrow gate the night of the murder — a detail erased from the trial record. Vesper's POV. Beat: cold dread; the company helped bury something, and Vesper still works for it.

chapters.title: The Heirs' Dinner
chapters.summary: Vesper attends the Harrow anniversary rehearsal under pretext of arranging transport, meeting the heirs: son Aldous, daughter-in-law Mireille, and the patriarch Edmund, whose dementia seems performed rather than real. Vesper's POV. Beat: theatrical menace beneath polite crystal and candlelight.

chapters.title: Deacon Sees Something
chapters.summary: Deacon, moonlighting as a delivery boy at the estate, spots Edmund lucidly shredding documents late at night. Deacon's POV. Beat: fear and loyalty colliding — he wants to protect Vesper but knows telling them paints a target on his back.

chapters.title: A Will That Waits
chapters.summary: Ruthie reveals she witnessed an unsigned codicil to Eleanor's will years ago, one that disinherits everyone if 'the truth of my death surfaces.' Vesper realizes the inheritance depends on the old verdict standing. Vesper's POV. Beat: the theme crystallizes — the murder isn't past; it's being maintained.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Silence
chapters.summary: Okonkwo admits he drove the erased cab that night and was paid to forget the passenger: a young woman leaving the estate, alive. His guilt has kept him driving nights ever since. Okonkwo's POV. Beat: confession as relief and rupture; the found family strains under old debts.

chapters.title: Someone Tails the Tail
chapters.summary: Vesper notices a gray sedan following their surveillance runs — hired muscle, or police? A near-miss on the river road ends with Vesper's brake line tampered. Vesper's POV. Beat: the investigation turns physical; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: Letters From Cell Block D
chapters.summary: Marcus finally breaks his silence through smuggled letters: he saw who left the estate that night and confessed to protect her. He names no one, but describes a ring — Mireille's engagement ring, worn by someone else. Vesper's POV. Beat: hope curdling into horror at what protection cost.

chapters.title: Mireille's Version
chapters.summary: Mireille approaches Vesper first, offering money to stop digging, then, when refused, a partial truth: she found Eleanor dying and stayed silent to protect Aldous. Mireille's POV. Beat: complicity dressed as love; the reader starts doubting every heir.

chapters.title: The Ghost Lawyer's Files
chapters.summary: Vesper and Deacon break into the dead lawyer's storage unit and find Edmund commissioned the original 'proof of innocence' — meaning the client hiring Vesper now is Edmund himself, testing whether his secret holds. Vesper's POV. Beat: vertigo; the puppeteer wants an audience.

chapters.title: Aldous Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted with the tape, drunk Aldous confesses he argued with Eleanor that night but swears she was alive when he left — and that Edmund told him to say otherwise. Aldous's POV. Beat: a weak man's collapse; the patriarch's control revealed as the true crime scene.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Preparations for the dinner accelerate; Edmund announces he'll make 'a final declaration' regarding the estate. Vesper realizes the new murder the client paid to prevent may be Edmund silencing everyone who knows. Vesper's POV. Beat: countdown pressure; every ally is now a potential victim.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Debt
chapters.summary: It emerges Ruthie was the young woman in Okonkwo's cab — Eleanor's confidante, carrying the codicil — and that Edmund has been blackmailing her for a decade. Ruthie's POV. Beat: shame transformed into resolve; she chooses to testify despite everything.

chapters.title: The Gray Sedan Closes In
chapters.summary: Edmund's fixer abducts Deacon to flush out the evidence. Vesper trades the dispatch tape for Deacon's release, secretly keeping a copy hidden in the cab company's dead-letter drawer. Vesper's POV. Beat: sacrifice and cunning; the found family becomes the operation.

chapters.title: Dinner Is Served
chapters.summary: The anniversary dinner begins. Vesper infiltrates as the hired driver while Okonkwo, Ruthie, and Mireille hold positions. Edmund rises to speak. Vesper's POV. Beat: taut suspense, every toast a loaded gun.

chapters.title: The Declaration
chapters.summary: Edmund, feigning confusion, publicly rewrites the will and re-closes the case — until Vesper plays the dispatch tape and produces the codicil, forcing the room to hear Eleanor's conditions read aloud. Climax: Edmund drops the act and threatens violence. Vesper's POV. Beat: the mask shatters.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Edmund's fixer turns on him when the money dries up; the heirs, given the choice between covering for the patriarch and the truth, choose truth. Police arrive to find a signed confession dictated by Edmund himself, believing his lawyer present. Vesper's POV. Beat: catharsis without triumph — the law gets its man by accident.

chapters.title: Exoneration
chapters.summary: Marcus walks free after ten years. Father and child meet outside the prison gates; he asks why Vesper never stopped, and Vesper answers: 'You were my alibi too.' Quiet reconciliation, imperfect but real. Alternating Vesper and Marcus POV. Beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Same Headset
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Vesper returns to dispatch, the found family gathered around the radio on a slow night. A new caller requests a prepaid fare 'to prove nothing happens' — and Vesper smiles, ready. Final beat: vigilance as love; the parish keeps its watch.
